tribe: Enslaved in the house of Abu Hudhayfa al-Makhzumi
teaser: The first blood spilled for this deen was a woman's. She owned nothing, and she gave everything, first.
quran_mention: They resented them for nothing but that they believed in Allah — Quran 85:8

layers.title: Who She Was
layers.subtitle: A name, a father's name, and nothing else recorded
layers.content:
The books that record her death give almost nothing about her life. Sumayyah bint Khayyat. She was enslaved in the house of Abu Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira ibn Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Makhzum — a Makhzumi noble, a man of the clan that produced Abu Jahl.

Ibn Sa'd tells the story from the direction of the men. Yasir ibn Amir arrived in Makka from Yemen with two brothers, searching for a fourth who had disappeared. The brothers gave up and went home. Yasir stayed and became Abu Hudhayfa's client. Abu Hudhayfa then married him to Sumayyah, the woman he owned. She bore Ammar, and Abu Hudhayfa freed the boy.

That is her biography before Islam, and it is somebody else's decisions from beginning to end. She did not choose the city, the household, or the husband.

We know she had at least two sons — Ammar and Abdullah ibn Yasir. We know her kunya, Umm Ammar. We do not know when she was born, what she looked like, or where in the world Khayyat was from. The first thing the sources let her do on her own account is believe.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: Seventh on a list of seven, and the only woman on it
layers.content:
Mujahid's report is one of the most quoted lines in the early history, and people usually stop reading it before the end. Transmitted through Mansur to Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid: the first of those who displayed Islam openly were seven — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Bilal, Khabbab, Suhayb, Ammar, and Sumayyah, the mother of Ammar.

Read the list again. Six men and one woman. A prophet, a wealthy merchant, and five people who between them owned almost nothing.

Ibn Sa'd records that the whole household came in together: Yasir, Sumayyah, Ammar, and Ammar's brother Abdullah. Al-Mubarakpuri says they embraced Islam in its early phase.

Mujahid then explains what protection meant in Makka. The Prophet's ﷺ uncle protected him. Abu Bakr's people protected him. As for the others — and this is the point of the whole report — there was nobody. A woman who was enslaved in the household of the clan leading the persecution had no relative to appeal to, no price anyone would pay, and no tribe that would take offence on her behalf.

She declared anyway.
layers.hadith_ref: Reported from Mujahid through Mansur — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Persecution)

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: She never reached Madinah. She met him on the road.
layers.content:
Everything the sources preserve of her time with the Prophet ﷺ happens in the open ground outside Makka, where the tortured were taken in the middle of the day.

Uthman ibn Affan described one of those walks. 'I came with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ holding my hand, walking on the flat, until we reached Abu Ammar, Ammar and his mother while they were being tortured.' Yasir said only, 'Time is like that.' And the Prophet ﷺ said, 'Be patient. O Allah, forgive the family of Yasir.'

Yusuf al-Makki's report has the Prophet ﷺ pass them in the same place and say: 'Good news, family of Ammar. You are promised the Garden.' Al-Mubarakpuri gives the wording as: 'O family of Yasir, be patient. You will certainly find your place in Paradise.'

That is the whole record. No years of companionship, no migration, no battles, no narrations she passed on. She was not addressed as an individual in any of it — she was addressed as part of a family, which is the way she was living and the way she would die.

She was promised the Garden while lying on burning ground, and she never saw a single day of the ummah's ease.
layers.hadith_ref: 'Good news, family of Ammar. You are promised the Garden' — reported from Yusuf al-Makki, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: Iron in the sun, and then Abu Jahl at evening
layers.content:
Mujahid describes the method. Those without protection were taken out, put into iron coats of mail, and left in the sun until they reached their limit and said what they were asked to say. Others were then given water and carried back. Al-Mubarakpuri adds that the family of Yasir were repeatedly made to lie on the burning sand and beaten.

Iron does not shade a body. It stores heat and delivers it back.

Then the report turns to a single evening. Abu Jahl came, and he began by abusing and insulting her — she was worth mocking before she was worth killing. Then he stabbed her and killed her.

Ibn Sa'd's sentence after that is six words long: she was the first martyr in Islam. Al-Mubarakpuri, working from Ibn Hisham and Ibn Sa'd, writes that Abu Jahl killed her himself and that she thereby merited the title of the first woman martyr in Islam.

Her husband Yasir did not survive the persecution either; al-Mubarakpuri records that he died of the unrelenting torture. Their son Ammar was broken into saying words he did not mean, and an ayah came down to absolve him.

Of the four in that household, she is the one who did not bend and did not survive.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 85:8 — «وَمَا نَقَمُوا مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا أَن يُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ» — 'And they resented them for nothing except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy'
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III (from Mujahid); al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ called her son by her name
layers.content:
There is a small thing in the hadith literature that is not small. When the Prophet ﷺ spoke to Ammar about what was coming for him — at the building of the mosque, with the dust of the bricks still on Ammar's head — he did not call him son of Yasir. Umm Salama, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Abu Qatada and Abdullah ibn Amr all transmit the same address: ibn Sumayya. Son of Sumayyah.

In a society that measured a man by his father and his father's fathers, the Prophet ﷺ attached her son to her. Every time the warning was repeated, her name was repeated with it.

Abu Jahl, who killed her, was struck down at Badr by two brothers of the Ansar, Mu'awwidh and Awf, the sons of Afra, and finished by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. He did not live to see the city change hands.

One caution for the honest reader: Ibn Sa'd also preserves a report of a marriage of a Sumayyah to a man named al-Azraq, freed at Ta'if years later, which is difficult to reconcile with the account of her killing in Makka. The sources are not uniform on this, and Ibn Sa'd transmits both without resolving them.

What is not in dispute is the order. The first person to die for this deen owned nothing and had no one. She went first, may Allah be pleased with her.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 3:169 — «وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتًا بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ» — 'Do not think those killed in the way of Allah are dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, provided for'
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ addressing Ammar as 'ibn Sumayya' — narrated from Umm Salama, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Abu Qatada and Abdullah ibn Amr, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

quiz.prompt: What distinction do the early sources give to Sumayyah bint Khayyat?

options.text: The first woman to make hijrah to Abyssinia
The first martyr in Islam
The first woman to memorise the Qur'an
The first woman to give the bay'ah at al-Aqaba

quiz.citation: Mujahid, reported through Mansur, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Sa'd states it in a single line with no elaboration: she was the first martyr in Islam. Al-Mubarakpuri gives it as the first woman martyr. Either way, she was at the front.

options.text: Umayya ibn Khalaf
Abu Lahab
Abu Jahl
Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira

quiz.citation: Mujahid, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: The report says he came in the evening, abused and insulted her first, and then stabbed her. He was a chief of Banu Makhzum — the very household she was enslaved in.

quiz.prompt: In Mujahid's list of the first seven to display Islam openly, what is notable about Sumayyah?

options.text: She was the only woman named
She was the only one from Quraysh
She was the only one who had a protector
She was the only one who later emigrated

quiz.citation: Mujahid's list of the seven, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The list runs: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Bilal, Khabbab, Suhayb, Ammar, and Sumayyah. She stands in that sequence by name, not as somebody's mother or wife.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when he passed the family of Yasir being tortured on the open ground?

options.text: 'Fight back, and Allah will aid you'
'Say what they ask and keep your faith hidden'
'Good news, family of Ammar. You are promised the Garden.'
'I will buy your freedom tomorrow'

quiz.citation: Yusuf al-Makki, reported from Abu Bishr, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Uthman ibn Affan witnessed a similar passing and reported the words as: 'Be patient. O Allah, forgive the family of Yasir.' He could not stop what was happening. He could tell them where it ended.

quiz.prompt: How did the Prophet ﷺ address her son Ammar in the famous warning at the building of the mosque?

options.text: 'Son of Yasir'
'Abu al-Yaqzan'
'Son of Sumayya'
'Client of Banu Makhzum'

quiz.citation: Narrated from Umm Salama, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Abu Qatada and Abdullah ibn Amr, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: In a culture built on the father's name, he was called by his mother's. Her name entered the hadith literature through the way her son was spoken to.

quiz.prompt: Almost nothing of her life was her own choice — not the city, the household, or the marriage. The one thing she chose was belief. What have you actually chosen?
quiz.slider_label: How much of your life you chose

options.text: Less than I like to think. Most of it was arranged around me.
My response to things, if not the things themselves
My faith is the one decision I know is mine
I am still working out which parts I inherited and which I chose

quiz.citation: Reflection on the biography of Sumayyah bint Khayyat in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: A person with no freedom of movement, property, or protection still had one uncontrolled space. Quraysh understood that, which is why they attacked it directly.

quiz.prompt: She died before Islam had a mosque, a city, or a victory. What does it take to hold to something whose ending you will not see?

options.text: Believing the outcome is not the point
Trusting the people who will still be standing after you
Being convinced enough that the timeline stops mattering
I find it very hard. I want to see results.

quiz.citation: Reflection on Sumayyah's death in the Makkan period, before the Hijrah
quiz.scholar_reflection: She never heard an adhan. She never prayed in a mosque. Everything you associate with the practice of Islam came after her, and none of it would have come the same way without her.

quiz.prompt: Abu Jahl insulted her before he stabbed her — the humiliation came first. Which is harder for you, injury or contempt?

options.text: Contempt. Pain ends; being made small stays.
Injury. I can absorb words.
It depends entirely on who it comes from
The two are the same act. One is just quieter.

quiz.citation: Mujahid's account of the killing of Sumayyah, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He needed to make her worthless before he could make her dead. The insult was not an addition to the killing. It was the preparation for it.

quiz.prompt: Her son survived by saying words he did not mean; she did not survive at all. How do you hold two family members who met the same pressure differently?

options.text: They are not comparable. Each was given a different weight.
The Qur'an excused him, so who am I to weigh them
Both are honoured. Only one is a lesson I could imitate.
I notice I instinctively rank them, and I want to stop

quiz.citation: Reflection on the family of Yasir — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III, and Quran 16:106
quiz.scholar_reflection: The same household produced a martyr, a man who died of his injuries, and a man whose coerced words became a mercy in the Book for everyone after him.

quiz.prompt: The sources give her a few lines and no description. What does it mean that the ummah's first martyr is almost undocumented?

options.text: It fits — she was overlooked in life, so of course in the records too
It is a warning about whose stories we bother to keep
The record that counts was never written by historians
Her few lines have travelled further than most people's biographies

quiz.citation: Reflection on the brevity of the sources concerning Sumayyah bint Khayyat
quiz.scholar_reflection: We do not know her age, her face, or where her father came from. We know the order she stood in. That turned out to be the only detail that would not be lost.
